bug_description.original: Detailed Report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=4769079506894848 Project: libxslt Fuzzing Engine: libFuzzer Fuzz Target: xslt Job Type: libfuzzer_asan_libxslt Platform Id: linux Crash Type: Invalid-free Crash Address: 0x6190000005ed Crash State: xmlFreeProp xmlFreeNodeList xmlFreeNode Sanitizer: address (ASAN) Regressed: https://oss-fuzz.com/revisions?job=libfuzzer_asan_libxslt&range=202203050604:202203060605 Reproducer Testcase: https://oss-fuzz.com/download?testcase_id=4769079506894848 Issue filed automatically.
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed` at `xmlFreeProp(tree.c:2117)` while `xsltFuzzXslt()` parsed the staged witness with `xmlReadMemory()`. The saved `poc` is a malformed XML/XSLT buffer that still reaches `xmlParseDocument`, defines internal general entities (`<!ENTITY a ...>`, `<!ENTITY aa ...>` are visible in the staged input), and later triggers `xmlParseReference()` on `&aa;`/`&a;` references in content. `xmlParseReference()` reparses the referenced replacement text with `xmlParseBalancedChunkMemoryInternal()`, whose temporary SAX2 attribute path preserves `localname` as a borrowed dictionary-backed `cur->name` when `ctxt->dictNames` is enabled. Because the chunk is not well formed, the detach block guarded by `ret == XML_ERR_OK` is skipped and cleanup frees the temporary pseudoroot in place. In `xmlFreeProp()`, `DICT_FREE(cur->name)` only reaches `xmlFree()` when `cur->doc->dict` is absent or does not own that pointer; the saved ASan sink proves that this free arm ran for a pointer inside xmlDict storage. The staged source does not disclose whether that happened because `dict == NULL` or because a different dictionary was attached at cleanup, so the rebuilt trace anchors the closed source-level root cause at this ownership check rather than claiming every borrowed dict pointer is freed. The staged libxslt patch only removes deprecated init calls and Stage 01 recorded `patch_resolves: false`, so it does not provide a source-level fix for this reproduced sink.

source.description: First project statement that consumes the attacker-controlled fuzz buffer and hands it to libxml2 as an XML document.
source.value_from: The exact staged `poc` is the buffer passed here. Visible strings in that saved input show a malformed XML/XSLT prolog with `<!ENTITY a ...>`, `<!ENTITY aa ...>`, and later `&aa;`/`&a;` references, which is sufficient to reach the entity-reference parser path.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. The `DICT_FREE` free arm executes on an attribute-name pointer that ASan shows lies inside an xmlDict string-pool allocation rather than a standalone heap string.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `xmlFreeProp -> xmlFreeNodeList -> xmlFreeNode`, and the freed address `0x6190000005ed` is 109 bytes inside a 1048-byte region allocated by `xmlDictAddString`.

root_cause.description: Cleanup decides ownership from `cur->doc->dict`; on the crashing path that ownership check falls through to the free arm even though the name pointer is backed by xmlDict storage.
root_cause.note: Earlier steps only show that the attribute keeps a borrowed dict-backed name. The saved ASan sink is what proves the `DICT_FREE` predicate fails for this specific attribute, and the staged source does not reveal whether the failing case was `dict == NULL` or a mismatched dictionary.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled internal-entity replacement text is handed to the balanced-chunk parser, which builds the temporary partial subtree later freed on the error path.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The staged witness defines internal general entities and later references them in content; when one is expanded, `ent->content` is the exact malformed replacement text reparsed here.

parser_admitted.description: The malformed witness is nevertheless admitted as an XML document far enough to parse the DOCTYPE/internal subset and define internal entities before entering element-content parsing.
parser_admitted.condition: The saved `poc` contains a `<!DOCTYPE ... [<!ENTITY a ... <!ENTITY aa ...]>` prolog in its printable substrings, and the observed stack continues through `xmlParseDocument -> xmlParseElement -> xmlParseContentInternal -> xmlParseReference`.

entity_reference_reached.description: Document content contains a general-entity reference, so control takes the entity-expansion path instead of ordinary character-data parsing.
entity_reference_reached.condition: The saved input shows `&aa;`/`&a;` substrings, and the ASan project stack includes `xmlParseReference` immediately below `xmlParseContentInternal`.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzz target passes the attacker-controlled buffer into `xmlReadMemory()`, which admits the malformed witness as an XML document.
The admitted document defines internal general entities and later reaches `xmlParseReference()` on an entity reference in content.

The referenced entity replacement text is reparsed in a temporary chunk parser that shares the outer parser dictionary and document, and the temporary attribute-construction path keeps a borrowed dictionary-backed name pointer.
Because the entity chunk is malformed, the detach block is skipped and cleanup frees the temporary pseudoroot with its partial subtree still attached.
The sink is only reached because `xmlFreeProp()` evaluates `cur->name` as not owned by the current `cur->doc->dict`, so `DICT_FREE` falls through to `xmlFree()` on dict-backed storage.

fine_trace.note: Source. `xsltFuzzXslt()` passes the exact testcase buffer into libxml2. The saved input's printable substrings show internal entity declarations and later entity references, so this call admits the malformed witness to the XML parser.

When content parsing reaches an internal general-entity reference from the attacker document, libxml2 takes the internal-entity arm and reparses the referenced replacement text `ent->content` as a balanced chunk.

depends_on.via: parsed XML buffer contains internal entities and `&...;` references

fine_trace.note: The temporary chunk parser is initialized to reuse the outer parser's dictionary, SAX handler, outer document, and dict-names mode. This makes names created while parsing the entity chunk borrowed xmlDict pointers rather than standalone heap copies. ASan's allocation stack (`xmlDictAddString -> xmlDictLookup -> xmlDetectSAX2`) matches this shared-dictionary setup.

depends_on.via: `ent->content` is reparsed in the temporary chunk parser

fine_trace.note: While the malformed entity chunk is being parsed, the temporary attribute-construction logic keeps the name as the borrowed `localname` pointer whenever `ctxt->dictNames` is enabled. The saved artifacts do not show whether the free-list arm or the `xmlNewNsPropEatName()` arm ran, but both dictNames arms preserve the borrowed dictionary-backed name pointer that later appears in `cur->name`. This step alone does not explain the bad-free until cleanup evaluates the pointer against the current document dictionary.

The replacement text is not well formed, so `ret != XML_ERR_OK`. The detach block guarded by `ret == XML_ERR_OK` is skipped, leaving the partially built subtree still attached under the temporary pseudoroot instead of being detached into `*lst`.

depends_on.via: temporary subtree with partially built attributes

fine_trace.note: Error cleanup frees the temporary pseudoroot with its partial children still attached, so recursive teardown descends into the malformed attribute subtree instead of returning it as a detached node list.

`xmlFreeProp()` loads the current document dictionary and `DICT_FREE` only calls `xmlFree()` if that dictionary is absent or `xmlDictOwns(dict, cur->name) == 0`. The saved ASan sink proves that this specific `cur->name` satisfied that predicate even though its bytes came from xmlDict storage. The staged artifacts do not reveal whether the failure was `dict == NULL` or a mismatched dictionary, only that cleanup evaluated the name as not owned by the current document dictionary.

Sink. Recursive cleanup reaches the `DICT_FREE` free arm and calls `xmlFree()` on `cur->name`. ASan shows this address is inside an xmlDict allocation from `xmlDictAddString`, so it is not a standalone heap string that may be passed to `free()`.

allocation_context.note: ASan says the freed address came from `xmlDictAddString -> xmlDictLookup -> xmlDetectSAX2` during document parsing. This grounds the trace's claim that `cur->name` is backed by dictionary storage rather than by a standalone heap allocation, but it does not by itself identify why `xmlFreeProp()` later treated the pointer as not owned by the current `cur->doc->dict`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: allocation_context confirms the name came from xmlDict storage; the rebuilt root-cause step adds the sink-side ownership failure that ASan alone does not localize.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` only removes deprecated libxml2 init calls in libxslt, and Stage 01 recorded `patch_resolves: false`. The reproduced bad-free is therefore grounded by the vulnerable libxml2 parser/tree path rather than by a validated patch hunk.

poc.trigger: The staged witness is fed directly to the `xslt` fuzz target, whose `xsltFuzzXslt()` helper calls `xmlReadMemory()` on the buffer. The saved run reproduces the ASan bad-free in `xmlFreeProp` with this exact file.

format.name: malformed XML/XSLT
format.contract: A malformed XML/XSLT buffer that is still admitted by `xmlReadMemory()` far enough to define internal general entities in the DOCTYPE and later reference one from document content, so `xmlParseReference()` reparses malformed replacement text and teardown reaches `xmlFreeProp` on a temporary partial subtree.
